reason: Portal vascular disease supports cardiovascular and hepatic primary axes. Common congestive hypersplenism with cytopenias supports haematologic involvement; gastrointestinal symptoms alone do not add an axis.

Red-cell aplasia and mandibulofacial dysostosis define the primary axes. Cleft palate and conductive hearing impairment each occur in 2/2 patients, supporting gastrointestinal and otologic involvement.
The tumor originates in kidney, supporting renal alone. Sarcoma histology does not establish locomotor tissue involvement, and distant metastases do not meet the common-involvement threshold.
Origin in the superior vena cava establishes cardiovascular. Vascular smooth muscle is outside the musculoskeletal axis; the ancestry alone does not establish infection.
This is a blood and marrow leukemia. B-cell lineage and lymphoma ancestry do not independently establish infection, immunodeficiency, autoimmunity or a lymphoma diagnosis.

Staphylococcal toxin-mediated shock defines infectious_immune and cardiovascular. Common acute kidney injury and thrombocytopenia support renal and haematologic involvement; the four-axis cap permits omitting hepatic dysfunction.

Neurologic impairment, skeletal defects and cleft palate/GI anomalies are defining manifestations. Unspecified genitourinary anomalies do not establish renal disease, and reported infections do not establish intrinsic immunodeficiency.
